title: Ringed direct image commutes with derived completion, with its unit normalization
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_X),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Y),R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites: its inverse image $f^{-1}$ preserves finite limits and is left adjoint to $f_*$, and its ring map is $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, where the $R_T$ are sheaves of commutative rings. Let $\mathcal J_Y\subset R_Y$ be an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections, and let $\mathcal J_X\subset R_X$ be the ideal generated by its image. Use the unbounded module derived categories $D(R_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $Rf_*:D(R_X)\to D(R_Y)$ be total right derived module direct image, computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; module direct image and its ring action are as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

Write $\Lambda_T:D(R_T)\to D(R_T)$ for the left-adjoint reflection into locally derived $\mathcal J_T$-complete complexes, with unit $\eta_T$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. Here locally complete means that for every site object $U$ and $a\in\mathcal J_T(U)$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{R_T|_U}(R_T|_U[1/a],M|_U)$ is zero; localization is sheafified sectionwise localization [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $Rf_*$ sends locally derived $\mathcal J_X$-complete objects to locally derived $\mathcal J_Y$-complete objects. For every $M\in D(R_X)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_{f,M}:\Lambda_Y(Rf_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*(\Lambda_X M).$$
It is the unique arrow satisfying
$$\gamma_{f,M}\circ\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}=Rf_*(\eta_{X,M}).$$
There is no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis on $M$, no Noetherian hypothesis on the ring sheaves, and no assumption that $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A0G, label lemma-pushforward-commutes-with-derived-completion (including the unit-normalized canonical map in its proof); preservation of complete objects is label lemma-pushforward-derived-complete, Tag 099J.

proof.text: The source ideal is locally finitely generated: inverse image carries a covering epimorphism onto the target ring to a covering epimorphism, and the images of each finite generating list generate its image ideal. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-site-presentation] to obtain $e\circ f\cong h\circ g$ with $g,e$ ringed equivalences and $h$ induced by a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. The module-equivalence lemma [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] gives exact derived equivalences and identifies the local Hom tests, hence the full subcategories of locally complete objects. Completion exists by [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. An equivalence $E$ identifying these subcategories carries the unit to a reflector unit: for complete $L'$, $\operatorname{Hom}(E\Lambda M,L')=\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda M,E^{-1}L')=\operatorname{Hom}(M,E^{-1}L')=\operatorname{Hom}(EM,L')$. Thus there is a unique unit-preserving isomorphism $E\Lambda\cong\Lambda' E$. The derived composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies $e_*Rf_*$ with $Rh_*g_*$. Conjugating an arrow and its unit equation by these equivalences preserves existence, uniqueness and invertibility. It suffices to prove the assertions for $h$; rename it $f$.

source.place: Tag 099J, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete, opening reduction; Tag 0A0G, construction of comparison

proof.text:
Suppose $M$ is locally $\mathcal J_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. For $V\in\mathcal D$, $a\in\mathcal J_Y(V)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, put $U=u(V)$ and $a'=f^\sharp(a)\in\mathcal J_X(U)$. The slice formulas and localized-ring pullback in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], with the derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_Y|_V)}(R_Y|_V[1/a],(Rf_*M)|_V[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X|_U)}(R_X|_U[1/a'],M|_U[q]).$$
Local completeness makes the source-side internal Hom zero, so the sectionwise Hom formula [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] makes this group zero. The calculation applies to every object over $V$, using its restricted section and localized morphism.

source.place: Tag 099J, local Hom calculation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U

proof.text: Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_{R_Y|_V}(R_Y|_V[1/a],(Rf_*M)|_V)$. Its restriction to any $W\to V$ is the corresponding internal Hom by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The sectionwise formula [lem-sfb-derived-internal-hom-sections-model] and Step 2 give $H^qR\Gamma(W,H|_W)=0$ for all $q,W$. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $H$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The derived-evaluation identification [lem-sfb-unbounded-sections-localization] computes $R\Gamma(W,H|_W)$ by the actual section complex $I(W)$. Every cycle in $I^q(W)$ is a boundary, since its class is in this zero group. The cohomology presheaf is therefore zero, and so is its sheafification $\mathcal H^q(H)$ for all $q$. Thus $H=0$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], proving that $Rf_*M$ is locally complete.

source.place: Tag 099J, vanishing on all objects and shifts; Tag 08JA, section-RHom-over-U

proof.text: The object $Rf_*\Lambda_XM$ is complete by Step 3. The reflector bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model] gives a unique $\gamma_{f,M}:\Lambda_YRf_*M\to Rf_*\Lambda_XM$ with $\gamma_{f,M}\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}=Rf_*\eta_{X,M}$. For $M\to M'$, the two naturality composites out of $\Lambda_YRf_*M$ have equal composites with $\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}$ by naturality of the units. The same bijection makes them equal. This constructs the natural comparison with exactly the required normalization and uniqueness.

For a slice $V$, let $K_Y$ be the augmented complex of [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model]. Its restriction has the same augmented extended Cech local description for $\mathcal J_Y|_V$. The restriction comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies $(R\mathcal Hom(K_Y,N))|_V$ with $R\mathcal Hom(K_Y|_V,N|_V)$ and identifies the maps induced by the augmentation. The reflector characterization in the Cech-model statement therefore identifies $(\Lambda_YN)|_V$ with $\Lambda_{Y/V}(N|_V)$, with its unit. The same argument applies on $X$ and further slices. This establishes localization compatibility without assuming that restriction commutes with arbitrary derived limits.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] on $M$ and $\Lambda_XM$, and Step 5 on both units. Restricting Step 4 gives $\gamma|_V\,\eta_{Y/V}=R(f_V)_*\eta_{X/u(V)}$. Uniqueness in Step 4 on the slice identifies $\gamma|_V$ with $\gamma_{f_V,M|_{u(V)}}$. For invertibility, take its cone. Exact restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] identifies its cohomology with restricted cohomology sheaves. If these vanish on a covering family of each target object, every section of every cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on that cover and is zero by sheaf separatedness [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The cone is then zero. Since $\mathcal J_Y$ is locally finitely generated, it suffices to work on slices with $\mathcal J_Y=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$, where its image ideal is $(c_1,\ldots,c_r)$ for $c_i=f^\sharp(b_i)$.

source.place: Tag 0A0G, local reduction after construction of comparison

proof.text: On such a slice put $Q_n^Y=\bigotimes_i[R_Y\xrightarrow{b_i^n}R_Y]$ in degrees $[-r,0]$ and $Q_n^X=\bigotimes_i[R_X\xrightarrow{c_i^n}R_X]$. Take the strict transitions $(b_i,1)$ and $(c_i,1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$ and degree-zero chain maps $z_n:R_Y[0]\to Q_n^Y$, $z'_n:R_X[0]\to Q_n^X$ from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. That statement identifies $\Lambda_YRf_*M$ and $\Lambda_XM$ with the strict total derived limits $L_Y S_\bullet$ and $L_X T_\bullet$ for $S_n=Rf_*M\otimes^L Q_n^Y$, $T_n=M\otimes^L Q_n^X$, with exactly the units induced by $z_n,z'_n$. The representative-independent strict-tower comparison and its unit normalization are also explicit in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-cech-koszul-dual-limit].

The K-flat pullback computation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify $Lf^*Q_n^Y$ with $Q_n^X$: the entries $b_i^n$ of each finite free differential become $c_i^n$. The transition $(b_i,1)$ becomes $(c_i,1)$, and the degree-zero map $1$ remains $1$. Tensoring these identities gives identifications of the entire augmented strict Koszul towers, including their tensor-differential signs, since transitions have degree zero. The explicit two-term factors, transitions and units used here are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector].

source.place: Tag 0A0G, final Koszul-pullback identity; explicit transition calculation

proof.text:
The complex $Q_n^Y$ is bounded with finite free terms, so it carries the strict-perfect package $i_r=p_r=\mathrm{id}$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], whose arrow $\pi_{f,M,Q_n^Y}$ is the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_M\otimes1)$ after the canonical tensor/pullback comparison, i.e. the projection transformation $\alpha$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] at $P=Q_n^Y$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] it is an isomorphism $\alpha_n:S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*T_n$ (with $Lf^*Q_n^Y=Q_n^X$ from Step 8). Naturality of the canonical projection transformation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], applied to the transitions $t_n^Y,t_n^X$ identified in Step 8, gives the actual equation
$$Rf_*(1_M\otimes t_n^X)\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_n(1_{Rf_*M}\otimes t_n^Y).$$
Its naturality at $z_n:R_Y[0]\to Q_n^Y$ and its tensor-unit equation $\alpha_{M,R_Y}=1$ give $\alpha_n(1\otimes z_n)=Rf_*(1\otimes z'_n)$. These are the Koszul-transition and levelwise-unit squares.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula; Tag 0A0G, levelwise comparison and transition refinement

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-projection-morphism] to the augmented finite free tower $P_\bullet=Q_\bullet^Y$. Step 8 identifies its pullback with $Q_\bullet^X$, with the actual transitions and units. The resulting $u:S_\bullet\to Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}T_\bullet$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(R_Y))$ evaluates to the specific $\alpha_n$ of Step 9. For $a_{f,T}:Rf_*L_XT\cong L_YRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}T$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], set $\delta=a_{f,T}^{-1}L_Y(u)$. The use of an actual strict derived-tower morphism supplies the coherent derived-limit map and its connecting square.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, tower-topos proof; Tag 0A0G, passage to limit

proof.text: Every evaluation of $u$ is invertible by Step 9. Kernels and cokernels in the tower category are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], hence so is cohomology. The cone of $u$ has zero cohomology at each index, thus zero cohomology as a tower object. Therefore $u$ is invertible in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(R_Y))$. The exact functor $L_Y$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] preserves its inverse. Since $a_{f,T}$ is invertible, so is $\delta$. This does not require exact countable products.

source.place: Tag 0A0G, derived-limit isomorphism; levelwise cohomology argument

proof.text:
The augmented-tower equation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-projection-morphism] is $L_Y(u)\zeta_Y=a_{f,T}Rf_*(\zeta_X)$. The unit-preserving Koszul identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] give $\zeta_Y=\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}$ and $\zeta_X=\eta_{X,M}$. Hence
$$\delta\eta_{Y,Rf_*M}=a_{f,T}^{-1}L_Y(u)\zeta_Y=Rf_*\eta_{X,M}.$$
The reflector bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model], with complete target $Rf_*\Lambda_XM$ from Step 3, identifies $\delta$ with the unique $\gamma_{f,M}$ of Step 4. Thus that specific comparison is invertible on each generating slice, globally by Step 6, and in the original presentation by Step 1. The unit equation and naturality were already proved in Step 4. The argument allows the empty Koszul list and places no boundedness condition on $M$.
